newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan palladium premiums edge up on Russian factor.
newsitem.headline: Japan palladium premiums edge up on Russian factor.

text.p: Japanese premiums of palladium have firmed slightly, as Japanese traders expected January deliveries of platinum group metals from Russia to be cancelled reflecting the delay in Japan's year-end export talks with the country, traders said on Wednesday.

In Tokyo's spot market, premiums of palladium sponge (used mainly in autocatalysts) inched up to about $2 per ounce on a c&f basis over the world benchmark, or loco Zurich, compared with about $0.50 premiums in early October.
Premiums of palladium ingot (used in the electronic parts sector) rose to about $1, up from a slight discount in early October.
"The domestic palladium market has been tightening slightly, backed by growing views that January delivery of platinum group metals will be skipped," a trading house trader said.

Russia's platinum group export agency, Almazjuvelirexport, or Almaz has informed some Japanese traders it could not guarantee January shipments due to a delay in the approval of the Russian state budget.
Traders said Japanese end-users whose percentage of long-term contract is higher, would need to cover a shortfall stemmed from an expected cancellation of January Russian deliveries in the market.
They said palladium's sponge grade was particularly tight as demand from the auto catalyst sector in Europe remained firm.
One trader forecast domestic palladium price to stay firm at least until the end of January.
Japan is the world's largest consumer of platinum group metals.
According to Finance Ministry's data, Japan imported 7.175 tonnes of palladium in October this year, and of these, 5.189 tonnes came from Russia.
Some 13 Japanese companies, including major trading houses and three bullion houses, have long-term contracts with Russia to import platinum group metals.
